Here is a list regarding general overall campaign expectations, a few ground rules, and other things that are relevant to this campaign.

**Book Source Policy**

The Pathfinder Core Rulebook (CRB) and Pathfinder Advanced Player's Guide (APG) are considered core books; all features, items, spells, feats, etc, are always completely open to all characters. By default, all other books are considered restricted, where the options and other items in those books are not banned, *but if you want to access something in a different book than the two listed above, simply contact me with what you want, and I'll review it.* In general, I will tend to allow things as long as they are not obviously overpowered, or break the balance of the game (or party), or something along those lines. Even if there is an issue with what you show me, I will try and work with you to meet your concept while maintaining the balance of the game as best we can.

**Posting Policy**

**EDIT; 7-8-16**: SmallPotatoes suggestion of a separation by "scenes" which can encompass a single battle or an entire village. Essentially, when there is some separation between what is happening between scene to scene, that can be a cut from one scene to another. So, generally speaking, once the party moves on from a spot, replies will be directed to a new root post that will be made (generally by myself). In this way, we can sort by new in session threads and keep relevant things in the replies to the main post.

**"Session" Policy**

Rather than keeping a singular enormous thread which tracks the entire campaign, I intend to separate it into several threads, usually when a significant "cut", decision, or something along those lines has occurred. For instance, entering into a new dungeon that will probably take a decent amount of time; choosing to side with one faction over another; or in an obvious case, beginning a written module, as the first "adventure" will be.

**General Campaign Setup**

Level: Beginning at level 1; planned to go to level 20.

Starting gold: The average for your class. For the Paladin, this is 175 gold, for the Rogue, this is 140 gold, for the Oracle, this is 105 gold.

EXP Gain: EXP will not be tracked, per se; once the party has accomplished an appropriate amount, they will be told to level up their characters.

Hit Points: The HP for PCs will be max for each level, based on their HD. Animal Companions, Mount, Familiars, etc, will receive half their HD in HP.

This list may be revised as time goes on; such revisions will have the date noted.

**EDIT: 8-23-16** Here are a few more changes I have made for the sake of expedient gameplay, primarily related to combat.

Initiative will be public. If there are no objections, when a combat starts, I'll go ahead and roll for all characters and post the results. This does take a bit of the fun out of it (let's be honest, rolling is the fun part), but it makes things quicker than possibly having to wait some hours for one person to roll their initiative before we can begin. Naturally, as the GM, I'll also roll for all NPCs.

Some NPC defenses and stats will be made public, in a big departure from what I normally do when I GM. In this case, only Hit Points (HP), Armor Class (AC), and Combat Maneuver Defense (CMD) will be public since those are actively dealt with by the PCs frequently and it pays to know right away if you were successful or not. This is most useful if two players go back-to-back, as I'm sure will happen at least occasionally. There's no need to wait for me to see if a monster is still alive, or if he's tripped or not, or if you actually hit or not on your turn.

Other types of resistances, like spell resistance, resistances to various elements (fire, cold, etc), or other defenses that are not mentioned will not be made public, at least not right away. Once such a resistance/defense is discovered, it will be noted so that it can be tracked by players without having to wait on me. Note than an appropriate knowledge roll (typically Arcana, Dungeoneering, Nature, Religion, or The Planes) will give you guys some general information about creatures of the appropriate types based on the result of the roll. For simplicity, I will also roll this automatically at the start of a combat for all characters who have the appropriate skill and give you the information you have available.
